The Court made the following:
 ORDER:

The Criminal Petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (for brevity 'the BNSS') by the petitioner/Accused No.8 for granting of pre-arrest bail in connection with Crime No. 10 of 2025 of Vidapanakal Police Station, Anantapur District, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420, 468, 471, 120- B of Indian Penal Code (for short 'the IPC').
\
2.

The prosecution's case, in a nutshell is that on the incident was occurred in between 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2024 at Vidapanakal mandal, Ananthapuramu during 18 round social audit on record period of 2023-24 on the implementation of MGNREGS programme in Vidapanakal Mandal, the accused are criminal conspiracy together made criminal breach of trust as entrusted the work to them mi , misappropriated the amount which was MGNREGS funds in Palthur, Karakamukkala and R.Kottala Grama Panchayaths that they have usurped the scheme funds restoring the fraudulent means by creating fake job cards by entering the benami names in the existing job cards thereby siphoning off the EGS wage compounent fund into benami accounts and also diverting the housing beneficiaries wage payments to those benami job card holders accounts thereby cheated the funds for their wrongful gain.
Further the accused deleted the benami names from the existing job cards by misusing the login credential of PO/MPDO by them without the knowledge of MPDO/Programme Officer.

Therefore, the accused caused loss of Rs. 18,74,394/- to the above V Manjunath Alias Kamsala Manjunath vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118071754/

sentences.text: 3. Mr.R.Harish Kumar, the learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.8, submits that the petitioner has not committed any offence; he was falsely implicated in this case; he is the sole breadwinner of his family; he is ready to abide any condition to be imposed by this Court; and urged to grant pre-arrest bail to the petitioner/Accused No.8.

4. Per contra, Ms. P. Akila Naidu, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, opposed in granting of bail stating that investigation is not yet completed; if the petitioner is granted pre-arrest bail, he will interfere in the investigation, and it is urged to dismiss the bail petition.

5. Perused the record.
6.

In the F.I.R. there are specific overt acts against the petitioner/accused No.8 inasmuch as, the Mandal Parishad Development Officer in her report dated 08.02.2025 specifically attributed allegations against the petitioner that he being the Field Assistant of R.Kottala GP misappropriated the amount of Rs.54,514/-.
This Court does not deem it fit to grant pre-arrest bail to the petitioner.

Grant of Anticipatory bail is neither a license for the commission of an offence nor it is a shield or protection for a person against whom specific allegations are leveled, as per the decisions of the Flon'ble Apex Court in / Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Panjab^ and Sushila Aggarwal v. State of(NCT ofDelhi)^.
(1980) 2 see 565 ^2020) 5 see 1 7.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature and gravity of the allegations levelled against the petitioner, there are no merits for grant of pre-arrest bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
8. In the result, the Criminal Petition is dismissed.

However, as per the request of the learned counsel for the petitioner, liberty is granted to the petitioner to surrender before the learned Jurisdictional Court concerned within one (01) week from the date of receipt of copy of this order,
and move an appropriate application before the learned Jurisdictional Court concerned.

The learned Jurisdictional Court concerned is directed to dispose of the said application in accordance with law, on its own merits by giving due and sufficient opportunity to the learned Public Prosecutor concerned, and pass appropriate orders within a reasonable time, as far as possible preferably in two (02) days.
